monthly_review.summary: You've significantly increased intensity this month despite fewer runs, shifting toward more Zone 3–4 work and faster paces — a clear sign of targeted aerobic development. However, total volume has dropped sharply.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved (+0.17 m/sec per bpm) while average pace accelerated by 22 sec/km — indicating better physiological return on effort despite reduced volume.

goal_tracker.message: You need 21.7 more km across 5 additional sessions (avg 4.3 km/session) to match last month’s volume — achievable with 1–2 runs/week over the remaining 28 days.

insights.title: Efficiency gain reflects improved neuromuscular coordination
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.45 m/sec per bpm, supported by cadence increasing from 150 to 154 spm and ground contact time dropping from ~315 ms (last month avg) to 307–309 ms in your two most recent runs — suggesting tighter stride mechanics.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance signals aerobic threshold focus
insights.body: This month, 33% of time was spent in Zone 3 (vs 36% last month), but Zone 4 rose to 18% (vs 12%) — and Zone 1 collapsed to 16% (vs 4%). This sharp drop in easy-effort running risks under-recovery and limits mitochondrial biogenesis stimulus.

insights.title: Stride length variability correlates with pace changes
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 67.5 cm (4.4 km @ 10:08/km, HR 123) to 84.4 cm (2.8 km @ 7:36/km, HR 146), showing strong pace–length coupling — but vertical oscillation also rose (7.3 → 8.5 cm) at faster efforts, suggesting inefficiency at higher intensities.

insights.title: Low session frequency limits cumulative adaptation
insights.body: Only 2 runs in April so far (vs 7 in March) means weekly load is unsustainable for aerobic base maintenance — especially given VO2 max remains stable at 34.0 (up from 33.0), implying current intensity compensates only partially for volume loss.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run tomorrow at HR ≤135 bpm (use your March 19 HR of 123 bpm as anchor), focusing on cadence ≥152 spm and vertical oscillation <7.5 cm
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 1/2 time dropped to 45% this month (from 51% last month); rebuilding low-HR volume is critical to support recovery and capillary density.

recommendations.action: Add one 3 km 'form drill' session this week: 6 × 1-min strides at 4:48/km pace (456 sec/km — your March best) with full walk-back recovery, monitoring vertical oscillation and ground contact time
recommendations.reason: Your fastest recent run (Mar 29) had 8.5 cm vertical oscillation — lowering this improves efficiency at goal pace without raising HR.

recommendations.action: Perform a 45-min easy run on Day 3 of this week at avg HR 130–134 bpm, keeping cadence ≥153 spm and stride length between 75–78 cm (observed in your 6.0 km runs)
recommendations.reason: Your recent long runs show optimal stride metrics (77.25 cm, 319 ms GCT) — reinforcing these parameters at low intensity builds durable form habits.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish weekly rhythm with 3–4 runs, prioritizing low-HR aerobic foundation and embedding efficient stride metrics (cadence ≥153 spm, GCT <315 ms, vertical osc <7.8 cm) across all efforts.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run (5 km, HR ≤135 bpm)
Strides + form focus (3 km w/ 6×1-min fast intervals)
Easy aerobic run (45 min, HR 130–134 bpm, cadence ≥153 spm)
